doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Becoming a writer and arranger through word of mouth
summary: Levin explains he is mostly a hired gun in writing, got known by meeting people in the New York scene, where deals are made by handshake.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How did you get into the arranging, the composing, the writing of themes for people and all that? How do you make those contacts?

I’ve for the most part been a hired gun in those areas. I do — there’s a lot of writing that I do that I have done that’s for me direct with a client. The client can be a wide range of areas. Most often they’ve been through producers or production companies who know me, they’ve either used me as a musician or just know what I can do.
But in the very beginning did you — you started writing tunes? How did you get to be known as someone who could do that?
I mean you don’t have to tell me specifically but is it just meeting the right people?

I think so. It’s probably the same process as just going into the area as a musician and becoming an active musician. You just get into the scene, hang out with people, meet them, play with them, and everybody learns what the other guy can do or can’t do, does well or does not do well. Most of the music scene, it’s probably why so many of us stay poor, a lot of it is done by word of mouth, a lot of agreements are made with a handshake, musicians are not good businessmen generally.
